developPage.title: Write a plugin
developPage.intro: Plugins add new tools to AI WorkDeck so the AI can call your code from a conversation. This guide starts with a minimal working example and ends with submitting for review.
developPage.s1Title: First, decide: do you need a plugin or a Skill
developPage.s1Lead: The two are easy to confuse, and picking the wrong one wastes a lot of work. The difference fits in one sentence:
developPage.s1LeadStrong: if it takes code, write a plugin; if explaining it clearly is enough, write a Skill.
s1Rows: Call an external system’s API to fetch data
Have the AI write review comments in your firm’s format
Define the steps and deliverable structure for a type of matter
developPage.s1P2a: A Skill is plain text (a prompt plus trigger words): it goes live on submission with no review, and is much faster to write. If a Skill covers your need,
developPage.s1P2b: and skip the rest of this page.
developPage.s2Title: Run your first plugin in five minutes
developPage.s2P1a: A plugin is a Java project compiled into a JAR, plus a
developPage.s2P1b: , zipped up and submitted. You need JDK 21 and Maven.
developPage.s2P2: Download the template project above — it is itself a complete working example. Only two files matter. The first is the tool class:
developPage.s2P3Strong: The description in @Tool is written for the AI
developPage.s2P3: — it directly decides whether the AI calls your tool at the right moment. Writing "when to use it" is far more useful than "what this method does": the former is what the AI has to judge.
developPage.s2P4: The second is manifest.json, which describes what the plugin is:
developPage.s2P5Strong: Tool names must match on both sides
developPage.s2P5b: must equal the Java method name. If they differ, the tool fails to register and the AI cannot see it.
developPage.s2P7: Note the zip contains the files themselves — don’t nest an extra directory. Unzipping should reveal manifest.json directly, not a folder.
developPage.s3Title: Try it on your own machine before submitting
developPage.s3P1a: No need to wait for review. Copy the entire
developPage.s3P1b: directory into your local plugin folder and restart AI WorkDeck:
developPage.s3P2: Your plugin should appear under Plugin Marketplace → Installed. Enable it, then ask something in a conversation that should use your tool and see whether the AI calls it. If it doesn’t, the @Tool description most likely fails to explain when to use it.
s4Rows: Globally unique; lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. It can never change once published — it is how upgrades identify "the same plugin".
Semantic version. Every submission must be higher than the previous one, or it is rejected.
Shown on the marketplace card. Describe what it does for the user, not the implementation.
Author and project homepage. Optional but recommended — users judge trust by them.
The capabilities this plugin uses; see the next section.
Tool list. name must equal the Java method name; write the description so its purpose is clear.
JAR file names relative to the package root. ../ paths outside the package are not allowed.
developPage.s5Intro: Four optional values; declare what you use:
developPage.s5BoxP1: Plugins run in the same process as the host app, so undeclared behavior cannot be blocked technically — a tool that declares no permissions can still read files. The declaration is not a runtime restriction but
developPage.s5BoxP2: : we cross-check it against the JAR’s static scan. Declaring no network while referencing network APIs — or the reverse — gets the submission rejected.
developPage.s6P1: Every version is reviewed by a human, usually within one to two business days. An automated scan runs first, and its report sits next to your permissions declaration on the reviewer’s desk.
s6Rejects: Declared permissions don’t match the APIs actually called
Custom TrustManager or any other way of bypassing certificate validation
Hardcoded IP addresses, or data sent out over plaintext HTTP
Reflection into the host’s internal objects (database connections, config services, etc.)
Obfuscated or packed code, or anything that hides what the code does
Version number not higher than the previous one
developPage.s6P2: Once approved, the platform signs the whole package with its private key and clients verify the signature on install. After that, nobody — including us — can alter the package contents without re-signing.
developPage.s6P3: If a problem surfaces after release, we revoke that version. Clients pick up the revocation list, disable it automatically and notify the user.
developPage.s7Title: A promise to users — and a constraint on you
developPage.s7P1: Our users are lawyers, and their machines hold clients' confidential material. A plugin gets the same access as the host app — far beyond what it needs for itself.
developPage.s7P2: So review errs on the strict side, and rejections come with reasons. If your plugin genuinely needs a sensitive-looking capability, explain why in the submission notes — it makes review much faster.
developPage.s8Title: Web plugins: build the UI in HTML/JS
developPage.s8P1a: If what you want is an interface — a form, a lookup tool, a dashboard — you do not need Java. Put a
developPage.s8P1b: directory in the package (plain static HTML/JS/CSS, entry web/index.html) and point manifest
developPage.s8P1c: at it. It may ship no JAR at all.
developPage.s8P2: The desktop app loads a Web plugin into a sandboxed iframe, deliberately not same-origin: plugin scripts never see the host session, every capability travels over the postMessage bridge, and the host checks each call against the manifest permissions. Unlike a JAR plugin, this declaration is an enforcement boundary rather than a self-description.
developPage.s8SdkLead: web/awd-plugin-sdk.js in the template wraps that bridge. Nothing works before the handshake:
developPage.s8P3: Errors arrive as rejected promises with err.code: permission_denied when the manifest does not declare what the call needs, unknown_method when the host does not recognize it. files.read caps text at 5 MB (truncated becomes true), and storage caps each plugin at 64 KB total.
developPage.s8ThemeLead: The handshake context now carries theme ('light'|'dark') and themeTokens (a table of --awd-* CSS variables); the host also pushes { type: 'theme', theme, tokens } on every later switch. The SDK applies it automatically — setting data-theme, toggling the awd-theme-light/awd-theme-dark class, and writing each token as a CSS custom property — so plugin CSS can just use var(--awd-surface) with zero JS. For script-driven behavior, use awd.theme.get() to read the current value and awd.theme.onChange(cb) to subscribe. The host simulator has a light/dark toggle button in its header, so you can test both themes without installing the desktop app.
developPage.s8SimLead: The template also ships a host simulator, dev/host-simulator.html: it impersonates the desktop host, performs the handshake, serves every method with fake data, and logs each bridge message. Run a local static server and you can develop in a browser without installing AI WorkDeck.
developPage.s8SimNote: Opening it directly over file:// usually shows a blank frame — browsers refuse to load sandboxed child documents from file://. The server must not rewrite URLs either: npx serve enables clean URLs by default, redirecting /web/index.html to /web so the relative SDK reference 404s.

packSubmitPage.title: Submit a native pack
packSubmitPage.intro: A native pack carries the heavy resources code consumes: script runtimes, platform binaries, static assets. It runs outside the JVM and carries no prompts; plugins that declare a dependency on it pull it down at install time. Every version is reviewed by a human and signed by the platform.
packSubmitPage.warnTitle: Everything in a pack is executed by the host.
packSubmitPage.warnBody: Python scripts get interpreted and native binaries get spawned, so the trust level matches a JAR plugin. Native binaries offer nothing to cross-check against, so review comes down to provenance: give the upstream open-source URL and a reproducible build script in your notes. Anything unclear is rejected.
packSubmitPage.formatIntro: Paste the manifest draft first, then pick every component archive it declares. Archives upload one by one as a stream; acceptance checks run only once all of them are in.
packSubmitPage.rule1: The manifest is an unsigned draft: no publishedAt, no signature. The platform fills those in on approval.
packSubmitPage.rule2: id is 2-50 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens, and becomes yours once used. First-party reserved ids are refused.
packSubmitPage.rule3: version must be higher than the highest existing version of that id; platforms accepts only * / mac-arm64 / win-x64.
packSubmitPage.rule4: Each component size and sha256 must match the real file exactly, or the submission is refused.
packSubmitPage.rule5: Archives are tar.gz; materialise symlinks with --dereference. Limits: 5000 entries and 500 MB unpacked per archive, 300 MB per submission.
packSubmitPage.manifestHint: Every entry under components needs name / platforms / archive / size / sha256 / unpackDir.
packSubmitPage.noteHint: Say what it contains, which plugin consumes it, where the binaries come from and how to reproduce the build. This is the main basis for review.

items: Triggers should cover phrases users naturally type, including short forms. More is better than missing.

postpaid.title: Cloud usage and credit
postpaid.confirm: I accept these billing and cloud deletion terms.
postpaid.terms: Usage consumes eligible gifts, then wallet funds, then credit equal to eligible gifts in the current period. Subscription benefits remain; Pro includes 3 GiB. Uploads are free; storage is billed over 30 days and downloads by bytes sent, including retries. Above the credit limit, new paid work stops. A reminder follows after 72 hours; if the debt is not fully paid after 120 hours, personal cloud data is permanently deleted, including cloud-only files. Local files are untouched. Partial payment does not restart the clock. Top-ups repay debt first. Each overdue case permits one successful free export per object, with failed attempts capped at three times its size. Cleared cloud data cannot be restored by payment; resuming backup requires an explicit action.

updatesPage.title: Versioning & Updates
updatesPage.metaDescription: Release notes for the AI WorkDeck desktop app: what each version changes for legal drafting, plugins and add-ins, and how minor and major updates reach lawyers.
updatesPage.subtitle: Minor versions update in-app; major versions ship as full installers

scheme.title: Version numbering
scheme.body: AI WorkDeck versions read 0.X.Y: the second digit X is the major version, the third digit Y is the minor version. The two update differently.
scheme.majorHint: X changes = major release (e.g. 0.11 to 0.12): download the full installer from this site and install over the old version.
scheme.minorHint: Y changes = minor release (e.g. 0.11.1 to 0.11.2): applied automatically inside the app - no installer download needed.

minor.title: Minor updates (in-app patches)
minor.body: The app downloads a patch containing only what changed (typically under 10MB) in the background, then prompts you to restart. Patches are Ed25519-signed and hash-verified; a failed update rolls back automatically. You can also check manually under Settings - Software Update.

major.title: Major updates (full installer)
major.body: Major releases change runtimes and core components, so they require a full installer. Your documents, projects and settings live in your user directory and survive the reinstall untouched. The app notifies you in-app when a new major version is available.

offline.title: Offline and intranet environments
offline.body: Every release always ships a full installer. Where in-app updates cannot reach the network, downloading the latest full installer upgrades you across any number of versions in one step.

integrity.title: Update integrity
integrity.body: The update manifest is signed with the publisher’s Ed25519 key and verified against the public key built into the app; every patch file is additionally SHA-256 checked. If any check fails, the whole update is discarded - unverified content is never installed.

release0770.headline: Cloud sync recovery protection and account compatibility update
items: Adds account and client support for cloud pay-as-you-go usage. Availability is shown on the account page; installing this version does not automatically accept the new billing terms.

After a cloud cleanup or an account switch, the old upload queue is not re-uploaded automatically; you need to review the status and resume it explicitly. Local files are not affected by cloud cleanup.
Keeps subscription bonus credits and existing benefits, and improves verification of account and cloud status across devices.

release0760.headline: Easier recording follow-up and smoother work across devices
items: Create minutes, extract tasks with calendar scheduling and assignee links, or export transcripts to Word directly from a recording file.
More accurate model lists and availability; copy temporary web workspaces to continue working.
Improved account and subscription status synchronization across devices.
Choose a conversation model directly on the welcome page; the Baoqingtian lawyer QR sign-in entry is easier to find.
Choose which projects to commit before exiting; unselected changes are kept. Switching projects no longer prompts for a commit.
The evidence panel follows the open document and stays out of the conversation area when no document is open. Fixed occasional dark borders above and beside the editor.

release0750.headline: Bailian for China AI, MCP and legal workflow improvements
items: China platform AI uses Alibaba Cloud Bailian; international accounts retain OpenRouter. Account site determines the provider, with matching models, tools, context limits and billing. After China credential migration, older desktop clients must upgrade to 0.75.7.
Fixes an unexpected sign-in dialog when opening local files while signed out.
Independent MCP connections support JSON import, local stdio and OAuth. Improved multi-file context, paginated reading, import progress and timeout recovery.
New law, case and penalty reference cards and reading tabs. Litigation visualization connects to workbench conversations, with better output verification and PPT typing, deletion and slide insertion.
Fixed expired-login status; redaction recovery data is saved and linked automatically. Quick recording from the welcome page, improved Chinese input and translated title refresh.
Updated to Electron 45.1.0 and security dependencies. This is a full desktop update; mobile apps are released separately.
Apple silicon only; requires macOS 13 or later

why.title: If the project is open source, why does it charge?

steps.title: Open source, not-for-profit, free software
steps.body: The desktop app is open source under the AGPLv3 and the full source is public. Downloading, installing, using and modifying it is free, with no subscription and nothing held back — commercial customers install the very same build. The license is a legal distinction, not a different product. The project doesn’t make money selling software, and the 20% below isn’t a profit margin either.

steps.title: You pay the real cost of outside services, plus a flat 20%
steps.body: AI chat calls model APIs. Beyond that there are Qichacha company records, the PKULaw legal database, OCR, speech transcription, web search and financial data — all billed per call by outside vendors. We buy them centrally so you do not have to open seven accounts and sign seven agreements, but the bill is still yours to pay. We charge a flat 20% on top because payment channels charge wildly different fees: App Store purchases can cost 30% or more on top, WeChat Pay is a different rate again, and every other channel is different still. Pricing each channel separately would be unworkable and hard to explain, so we average it out at a flat 20% — and topping up on our own site, the cheapest channel, is the better deal.

steps.title: Fixed costs are fronted by the founder; any surplus is amortized first
steps.body: The fixed costs of keeping the site and back end running — servers, domain names — are not billed to users up front; the project’s founder fronts them instead. If the flat 20% leaves a surplus after channel fees and third-party costs, it goes first toward amortizing that up-front outlay — the servers and domains are, after all, shared infrastructure.

steps.title: What’s left after that is donated; the books are published twice a year
steps.body: Once the up-front outlay is fully amortized, anything left over is donated to a national charity. Every six months we publish the books and usage on our site and GitHub, with the donation receipts attached.

community.q: What is the Community Edition, and do I need a license?
community.a: The Community Edition is what you download here, and it is the same installer commercial customers get — the difference is legal, not functional. Individuals, and teams willing to meet the AGPLv3 conditions, need no license. You need an internal-use license only if your organization wants to run a modified build without publishing the source, or to write closed-source plugins and private integrations. Embedding the core in a product you sell requires an OEM license.

topup.q: What happens when the sign-up credit runs out?
topup.aWxpay: Top up any amount on your account page via WeChat Pay. There is no minimum and nothing renews automatically. Credits are then drawn down call by call at the vendor charge × 1.2 — you spend what you use, and the rest stays put. Topping up on our own site carries the lowest channel cost, and it’s the way we recommend.
topup.aStripe: Top up any amount on your account page via Stripe. There is no minimum and nothing renews automatically. Credits are then drawn down call by call at the vendor charge × 1.2 — you spend what you use, and the rest stays put. Topping up on our own site carries the lowest channel cost, and it’s the way we recommend.

negotiate.a: Every price is a public list price and the same for every customer, including the 20% on usage and the commercial license tiers. We don’t negotiate individual deals, and we publish our books every six months.

selfHost.q: Can I build it myself and self-host?
selfHost.a: Yes. The source is published under the AGPLv3, so you can build it, host it, and point the AI calls at your own model account — our hosted services are optional, not a condition of using the software. If you distribute a modified build, the AGPLv3 source obligations apply; organizations that would rather not take those on can buy a commercial license.

transparency.a: Yes. Every six months we publish our books and usage on GitHub and on this site, including user count, install count, revenue, the cost of each payment channel, other expenses and donation records.

vendors.q: What do the upstream services cost?
vendors.a: Unit prices are whatever each vendor currently lists on its official pricing page; we don’t publish a price list of our own, and your credits are drawn down at the vendor charge × 1.2. These are the outside services the app calls, with their official pricing pages.

mobileAssistantPrivacy.security: Network traffic uses HTTPS, and production access is limited to necessary personnel. No system is completely secure; we handle and notify personal-data incidents as applicable law requires.
mobileAssistantPrivacy.mobileIntro: This notice explains how {operator} handles personal data in AI WorkDeck for iOS, Android, HarmonyOS and the WeChat mini program, including accounts, capture, project files, cloud transfer and optional AI. Files transfer to your selected project; desktop local storage does not mean mobile files are never uploaded.
mobileAssistantPrivacy.platformDifferences: The device-permission and local-record details below describe Android. iOS and HarmonyOS can also keep permitted capture coordinates in local records; upload forms do not separately send coordinates or manifests, but original media may retain its own location metadata. The WeChat mini program does not call location APIs. Saving a system-album copy defaults to on in iOS and off in HarmonyOS and WeChat, subject to each app’s settings. iOS background recording uses system audio capabilities and Live Activities, rather than Android persistent notifications. Personal calendars and reminders on these clients do not read or write the system calendar.
mobileAssistantPrivacy.sessionStorage: Login sessions use Keychain on iOS, AssetStoreKit on HarmonyOS and WeChat local storage in the mini program. These different mechanisms should not all be understood as system-encrypted storage.
mobileAssistantPrivacy.title: 8. Optional AI features and content reports
mobileAssistantPrivacy.capture: Only after you enable capture organization or automatic naming do image thumbnails, sampled video frames, up to the first 30 seconds of audio and necessary text pass through the configured {provider} route to relevant image, audio or auxiliary model services. They generate filenames, tags and filing fields; audio transcripts may feed further organization. Results are stored with the filing. When disabled, ordinary capture and transfer follow the process above.
mobileAssistantPrivacy.processing: The assistant requires an active subscription, cloud-backup authorization and separate consent. Questions, necessary conversation history, authorized project summaries and necessary source text pass through our cloud to {provider} and the inference provider to generate answers. Necessary search queries may reach Qichacha or PKULaw.
mobileAssistantPrivacy.retention: Summaries, questions, answers and source references are stored in your cloud account. Disabling the assistant deletes summaries and assistant conversations, not original files. Starting a new conversation does not delete old records. You can also request deletion through this page’s account and data deletion channel.
mobileAssistantPrivacy.report: Content reports contain text you choose to submit and necessary account, platform, conversation and handling records. They support investigation and, where automated triage is enabled, may be processed by configured AI services. This reporting entry does not automatically attach full chats, project files or runtime logs.
